A1.justification: Both PDFs describe CoMoGaussian and contain readable main text and appendices, including all 11 figures and 10 tables. The methods, experiments, and derivations can be matched reliably across versions.

before.justification: v1 reports original CoMoGaussian evaluations, component ablations, trajectory visualizations, and training-time measurements, including per-scene results in the appendix.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experimental results in the main text and appendices, including benchmark comparisons, ablations, and per-scene evaluations.

M1.justification: Appendix Section 8 revises the specified width of CNN F's two convolutional layers from 64 to 32 channels, a limited change to the reported architecture. The neural ODE, rigid/CMR transformations, losses, and inference procedure remain unchanged. The PDFs do not establish whether the width revision reflects an implementation change or a documentation correction.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same Deblur-NeRF synthetic and real-world scenes, ExbluRF real-world scenes, and sharp NeRF-LLFF images. No dataset, task, or blur scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged within the corresponding benchmark, sharp-image, estimator-ablation, and speed comparisons. For example, BAD-Gaussians, Deblurring 3DGS, and BAGS retain their participation in the same reported comparisons.

E3.justification: Section 8 changes the reported CNN channel count from 64 to 32, revising a model-size setting. The stated 40,000 training iterations, nine sampled poses, training stages, loss weights, and evaluation metrics remain unchanged. No experimental rerun is established.

E4.justification: The transformation and orthogonality ablations, motion-estimator comparisons, pose-count sensitivity study, sharp-image tests, and trajectory visualizations are retained. Tables 3–6 and the corresponding appendix analyses test the same questions with unchanged evidence.

E5.justification: Both versions report point estimates without repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. No uncertainty-reporting practice is introduced or revised.

E6.justification: Tables 1–10 retain their numerical entries, including benchmark scores, ablations, training times, and per-scene results. For example, CoMoGaussian PSNR remains 31.02 and 27.85 in Table 1 and 30.15 in Table 2. Qualitative examples and reported findings are also unchanged.

T1.justification: Appendix Section 13, Eq. (17), corrects the skew-symmetric matrix identity from W^3 = I to W^3 = -W, where W represents the unit rotation axis. This fixes a mathematical premise used in the subsequent Taylor/Rodrigues derivation; the resulting rotation and translation formulas remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The core contributions remain continuous camera-trajectory modeling with neural ODEs, rigid motion plus CMR refinement, and accurate reconstruction with real-time rendering. The state-of-the-art performance claim is retained without substantive strengthening or narrowing.

C2.justification: The explanations of CMR, estimator continuity, sharp-image generalization, and training-cost tradeoffs remain unchanged, as does Section 6's limitation concerning adaptive pose counts. The shortened conclusion omits the repeated static-object qualification, but that premise remains in the introduction and rigid-motion formulation.

D1.justification: Section 8 revises the CNN channel specification from 64 to 32. Other implementation disclosures, including kernel sizes, hidden dimensions, training schedule, loss weights, and RTX 4090 hardware, are retained. Moving the same project URL from the title area to the abstract does not change access information.

R1.justification: The same 42 references and substantive research positioning are retained. Related-work discussions and Appendix Section 10's distinction from SMURF remain unchanged; no cited work is added or removed.

P1.justification: v2 makes limited wording edits in the abstract, ablation discussion, and conclusion; simplifies the affiliation; and adds acknowledgements. It also harmonizes transformation notation and corrects Section 4.2's pose-composition reference from Eq. (1) to Eq. (5). The overall section structure is retained.

P2.justification: The title-page layout changes with the relocated project URL, and table spacing and text pagination shift. Section 4.4 now begins on page 6, and acknowledgements reflow the references. All figures and table structures are retained without new or removed displays.

improvement.justification: Correcting Eq. (17) removes a false algebraic premise from the rigid-body derivation, while the corrected cross-reference and notation improve clarity. These are limited but concrete improvements. The empirical evidence is unchanged, and the unexplained CNN-width revision does not establish an experimental or performance improvement.
